subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings & reranking (index scale & targets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightcart.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings & reranking (index scale & targets)

Samir / Elaine —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the items we agreed to validate next. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Top pain points you described:
- Search relevancy declines as catalog grows (esp. long-tail/skus with sparse metadata).
- Cost and latency spikes during peak merchandising events.
- Difficulty running low-latency reranking for session-scoped personalization without large infra costs.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Primary product DB: Postgres (metadata).
- Vector index: Milvus (self-hosted) for production; experimenting with Pinecone for smaller experiments.
- Current embedding model: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large for catalog items and queries.

Scale & patterns we captured:
- Index size: ~12M products today (images + text + sparse metadata), growing ~3–5% monthly.
- Vector dim: 1536.
- Batch patterns: nightly full refresh (~250k items/day processed as a bulk job) + hourly incremental updates (~4–6k items/hour).
- Online traffic: average ~120 QPS search traffic, peaks ~500 QPS during promos; typical session rerank set size: 10–30 candidates.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for BrightCart):
- Reranking end-to-end p95 latency < 120ms for a typical session (search + rerank).
- Average cost per end-user search (embedding + vector search + rerank) below your internal target (~$0.0006/query on avg).
- Quality improvement: measurable +5–10% lift in click-through/on-site conversions for head-to-mid queries in A/B test window.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) I’ll send a short eval pack (attached) with the sample query set you promised — that will let us run a like-for-like comparison.
2) Schedule a technical deep dive with Neha (SE) and your infra/ML lead to validate indexing workflow, KV cache needs, and SLOs.
3) Redwood will propose a 4-week POC plan (baseline metrics, config recommendation, and cost estimate).

Attachments: brightcart-discovery-notes.pdf (recap + sample schema), sample-query-set.csv (200 sample queries / test cases).

Proposed schedule: would Mon 7/27 or Tue 7/28 for a 60-min SE deep dive work for you?

Thanks — excited to dig in.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 17:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: BrightCart embeddings & reranking (index scale & targets)

Thanks Marissa — great write-up, captured most of it. A couple clarifications and a few extra data points from our infra side: 

- Index: 12.3M live SKUs (the 12M number you have is correct; includes variants). Growth: ~4% month-over-month.
- Vector store: Milvus currently (self-hosted on GCP). We have a smaller Pinecone eval index for a feature team.
- Embedding model: currently using OpenAI text-embedding-3-large for new content; legacy items use an in-house embedder (we're migrating).
- Typical rerank candidate set: 10–25 items per session; we do a cosine similarity search then a lightweight transformer-based reranker on top.
- Traffic: avg ~120 QPS (search), promos ~450–500 QPS sustained for 15–30 minutes.

Latency & cost targets (our priorities):
- Target p95 end-to-end rerank < 120ms (search + rerank). p99 target would be great but we understand that requires tuning.
- Cost: we’re aiming to keep avg per-search infra cost (embedding + search + rerank) under $0.0006 — if Redwood can get us within 25% of that while delivering reliability and output quality, that’s attractive.

On evaluation data: I attached the sample queries and added a small labeled set for relevance (sample-query-set.csv). We can also provide more labeled pairs if you need.

Next steps from our side:
- Monday 7/27 at 10:00am PT works for the deep dive with Neha and our infra lead (Elaine). Please send an invite.
- If the POC looks reasonable, we’ll pull procurement and infra folks into a follow-up to scope Dedicated / Private options.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
